- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% of recent mean.
- If model shows steady upward trend with low sentiment (≤0.3), it often over-estimates; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is rising while price is falling, model may lag; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >1.5σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is flat or declining, model often over-predicts; apply 1–3% downward correction if true outcome is <70% of forecast.
